body: Kim and Rhee, 'Price Limit Performance: Evidence from the Tokyo Stock Exchange' (Journal of Finance 52(2), 1997; ~380 citations), Tokyo 1989-1992: compared with stocks that came close to the limit without hitting it, stocks that hit their daily limit showed higher volatility on following days (volatility spill-over), continued price moves in the same direction (delayed price discovery) and higher volume after the limit (trading interference). Limits postpone rather than prevent the move. Deb, Kalev and Marisetty, 'Are Price Limits Really Bad for Equity Markets?' (Journal of Banking & Finance 34(10), 2010; ~55 Crossref citations) and 'Price Limits and Volatility' (Pacific-Basin Finance Journal 2017; Tokyo 2001-05 with propensity-score matching) find the costs overstated by Kim-Rhee's method: lower-limit hits show little volatility spill-over, and limits curb TRANSITORY volatility, though permanent volatility still spills over. Replicated: mixed; the magnet effect (prices accelerate toward the limit) is documented in China and Taiwan. India context: NSE/BSE apply stock-level bands (2/5/10/20%), with tighter bands and ASM/GSM surveillance on small and speculative stocks, so many Indian small caps hit consecutive circuits. Use for us: (1) a stock on lower-circuit can trap us for days, so position size must assume we cannot exit (liquidity is a survival variable); (2) a string of upper circuits on no news is the classic operator pattern (insight:lit-news-vs-no-news-momentum-frog-in-pan) and tends to reverse; (3) news-driven circuit hits keep moving after the band lifts.

data.dkm: limits curb transitory volatility; permanent spills over

title: Price limits/circuit filters: delayed price discovery and volatility spill-over (Kim-Rhee 1997); later work finds limits curb transient volatility (Deb-Kalev-Marisetty)

body: Federal Bank's SUE path (Q2 FY26 -1.11 quintile 1 -> Q2 FY27 +2.91 quintile 5) used reported consolidated EPS, which includes treasury income (Rs 238 cr in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 12-126 cr in prior quarters), one-offs (Rs 456 cr IT-refund interest in Q4 FY26, offset by a buffer provision) and a 60.6%-owned NBFC. The quintile happened to be robust (normalised EPS still a large beat), but for lenders the avoid-leg rule (L19) should be confirmed on (PPOP - normal credit cost) per share before it blocks a card. Untested: whether bank PEAD behaves like the full-sample result.
title: PEAD on banks: reported EPS mixes treasury gains, provision buffers and subsidiary profits - check SUE on core earnings before acting on a quintile

body: Fires on 19% of the frame; precision 32% vs 19.7% base; recall 32%. Unlike the US, not just a loss-maker proxy (S0 EBIT<0 alone lift 1.12 in India). Strongest broad Indian signal for liquidation/compulsory exit (O_strict lift 2.87 [1.88,4.11]). Excludes 20 of 91 >=3x winners -> deep-dive question, not a gate. S2b (<2.5x) lift 1.68, flags 32% of firms and 35% of winners.
title: India solvency back-test FY2016/18: S2 interest cover <1.5x -> QUESTION (lift 1.69 [1.27,2.20]; 2.87 on liquidation/exit) but cuts 20% of multibaggers; <2.5x variant no better
